- [ ] Inspect available clinical tables/schema
- [ ] Query monthly pediatric asthma ED exacerbation visits for last 3 years
- [ ] Query monthly oral steroid bursts for same cohort/window
- [ ] Assess fall/spring seasonality and summarize evidence

SELECT TOP 50 c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.vocabulary_id, c.concept_class_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM omop.drug_exposure de JOIN omop.concept c ON c.concept_id = de.drug_concept_id WHERE de.drug_exposure_start_date >= DATEADD(year, -3, CAST(GETDATE() AS date)) AND (LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%prednisone%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%prednisolone%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%dexamethasone%' OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%methylprednisolone%') GROUP BY c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.vocabulary_id, c.concept_class_id ORDER BY n DESC

WITH months AS (
  SELECT CAST(DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(DATEADD(month, -35, CAST(GETDATE() AS date))), MONTH(DATEADD(month, -35, CAST(GETDATE() AS date))), 1) AS date) AS month_start
  UNION ALL
  SELECT DATEADD(month, 1, month_start) FROM months WHERE month_start < DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(CAST(GETDATE() AS date)), MONTH(CAST(GETDATE() AS date)), 1)
), ed_exac AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT co.condition_occurrence_id, DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(co.condition_start_date), MONTH(co.condition_start_date), 1) AS month_start
  FROM omop.condition_occurrence co
  JOIN omop.concept cc ON cc.concept_id = co.condition_concept_id
  JOIN omop.person p ON p.person_id = co.person_id
  JOIN omop.visit_occurrence vo ON vo.visit_occurrence_id = co.visit_occurrence_id
  LEFT JOIN omop.care_site cs ON cs.care_site_id = vo.care_site_id
  WHERE co.condition_start_date >= DATEADD(month, -35, DATEFROMPARTS(YEAR(CAST(GETDATE() AS date)), MONTH(CAST(GETDATE() AS date)), 1))
    AND co.condition_start_date <= CAST(GETDATE() AS date)
    AND DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, COALESCE(p.month_of_birth,1), COALESCE(p.day_of_birth,1)), co.condition_start_date)
        - CASE WHEN DATEADD(year, DATEDIFF(year, DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, COALESCE(p.month_of_birth,1), COALESCE(p.day_of_birth,1)), co.condition_start_date), DATEFROMPARTS(p.year_of_birth, COALESCE(p.month_of_birth,1), COALESCE(p.day_of_birth,1))) > co.condition_start_date THEN 1 ELSE 0 END BETWEEN 5 AND 17
    AND (LOWER(cc.concept_name) LIKE '%exacerbation%asthma%' OR LOWER(cc.concept_name) LIKE '%acute%asthma%' OR LOWER(cc.concept_name) LIKE '%status asthmaticus%')
    AND (LOWER(cs.care_site_name) LIKE '% ed%' OR LOWER(cs.care_site_name) LIKE '%emergency%')
    AND LOWER(COALESCE(cs.care_site_name,'')) NOT LIKE '%l&d%'
)
SELECT CONVERT(varchar(7), m.month_start, 120) AS month, COUNT(e.condition_occurrence_id) AS pediatric_asthma_ed_exacerbation_visits
FROM months m
LEFT JOIN ed_exac e ON e.month_start = m.month_start
GROUP BY m.month_start
ORDER BY m.month_start
OPTION (MAXRECURSION 100)

Using OMOP EHR data, I found **partial support for spring peaks, but not consistent fall-and-spring peaks**.

Cohort/query definition:
- Children age **5–17**
- Asthma exacerbation ED visits: asthma exacerbation/acute asthma condition concepts linked to visits at care sites with `ED`/`EMERGENCY` in the care-site name

### Interpretation

- **ED asthma exacerbation visits:**  
  There are **spring elevations** in 2023–2024, especially **March/May**, but the pattern is not cleanly seasonal. Peaks also occur in **July 2023**, **December 2024**, and **January 2024/2025**. A consistent fall peak is **not evident**.

- **Oral steroid bursts:**  
  These show high counts in **winter/early spring** and some **late-summer/fall activity in 2024**, but not a reproducible fall-and-spring pattern across all three years. January/February and May are often high; 2025 shows a marked decline late in the year.

### Bottom line

**No — the data do not show a consistent fall-and-spring bimodal peak over the last three complete years.** There is some evidence of **spring/early-year elevation**, but **fall peaks are inconsistent**, and the sharp late-2025 drop suggests possible data-capture or cohort/ETL effects that should be checked before making a strong seasonal conclusion.
